37479.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37479.explanation:
A trade discount represents the reduction in cost of goods or services sold in the business environment. Trade discounts can help small businesses save money when purchasing goods or services from suppliers. Many suppliers require small businesses to pay within a specific time frame to receive the trade discount.

One of the main reasons why firms offer trade discounts is to encourage debtors to clear their outstanding balances quickly.

gross profit and increase cost of sales

37484.explanation:

37486.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37486.question_text: Which of the following is a book of ordinary entry?
37486.explanation:
Books of original entry refers to the accounting journals in which business transactions are initially recorded. The information in these books is then summarized and posted into a general ledger, from which financial statements are produced.

The main books of prime entry are:

  • Sales day book.
  • Purchase day book.
  • Sales returns day book.
  • Purchases returns day book.
  • Bank Book.
  • Cash Receipts Book.
  • Cash Payments Book.
  • Petty Cash Receipts Book.

37487.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37487.explanation: A balance sheet is a financial statement that reports a company's assets, liabilities and shareholders' equity.

37488.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37488.question_text: The process of entering transaction from one book to another is
37488.explanation: Posting in accounting is when the balances in sub-ledgers and the general journal are shifted into the general ledger.

37489.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37489.question_text: Which of the following is a trading account item?
37489.explanation: Carriage inwards is the shipping and handling costs incurred by a company that is receiving goods from suppliers. It is added to the cost of purchase and recorded in the trading account

37490.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37490.question_text: The addition of prime cost and factory overhead is
37490.explanation: The cost of goods manufactured equation is calculated by adding the total manufacturing costs; including all direct materials, direct labor (prime cost) and factory overhead; to the beginning work in process inventory and subtracting the ending goods in process inventory.

37492.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37492.question_text: Which of the following is an example of factory overheads?
37492.explanation:
Factory overhead is the costs incurred during the manufacturing process, not including the costs of direct labor and direct materials. 

Examples of factory overhead costs include: indirect materials, indirect labor, depreciation of the factory equipment and plant, amortization of patents, the cost of small tools used, factory utilities, insurance on the factory and equipment, property taxes on plant and equipment, property taxes on materials and goods

37493.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37493.question_text: Osa started business with Le 40,000 cash. The accounting entry is debit
37493.explanation: Debit capital account (i.e the money used in starting a business) and credit cash

37494.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37494.question_text: Branch stock account is used to determine the
37494.explanation:
This account records the transactions in regard to the stock in the branch at invoice price. The debit side of this account records the inflow of stock into the branch and credit side records its outflow from the branch.

The primary objectives of branch accounting are better accountability and control since profitability and efficiency can be closely tracked for individual locations. The head office is able to ascertain the profits and losses of each branch and compare results.

options.text: net value of goods sent to branch

37497.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37497.question_text: A partner who only make capital contribution but does not take part in the management of the partnership business is a/an
37497.explanation: Dormant partner is a partner who contributes capital and takes no share in the active business of a company or partnership, but is entitled to a share of the profits, and subject to a share in losses; They are also called sleeping partner or silent partner.

37498.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37498.question_text: which of the following is a component of prime cost?
37498.explanation: Direct materials are one of the main components of prime costs and include raw materials and supplies that are consumed directly during the production of goods. In production, electricity is required to aid the process. This makes it a part of the prime cost

37499.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37499.question_text: The concept which establishes the rule for the periodic recognition of revenue as soon as it is capable of objective measurement is
37499.explanation: The realization principle is the concept that revenue can only be recognized once the underlying goods or services associated with the revenue have been delivered or rendered, respectively. Thus, revenue can only be recognized after it has been earned.

37501.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37501.question_text: Which of the following is not an input device?
37501.explanation: In computing, an input device is a piece of equipment used to provide data and control signals to an information processing system such as a computer or information appliance. Examples of input devices include keyboards, mouse, scanners, digital cameras, joysticks, and microphones.

37502.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37502.question_text: The equivalent of income and expenditure account in a trading concern is
37502.explanation:
The income and expenditure account is an account prepared by non-trading concerns to ascertain surplus or deficit of income over expenditures for a particular period. Its equivalent is the profit and loss account . 

An income statement or profit and loss account is one of the financial statements of a company and shows the company's revenues and expenses during a particular period.

37503.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37503.question_text: The term used to denote the capital of a not-for-profit making organization is
37503.explanation: An accumulated fund is the capital fund of a nonprofit organization. Money is directed into the accumulated fund when revenues are greater than expenditures and there is a budgetary surplus.

37504.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37504.question_text: The portion of authorized capital that has been allotted to subscribers
37504.explanation: The Issued Capital refers to the number of shares issued by the company to the shareholders. In other words, the shares allotted or subsequently held by the shareholders is called the issued capital.

37505.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37505.question_text: Partners whose liabilities are restricted to their financial contribution to the partnership in the event of winding up are
37505.explanation: Limited partner is a partner in a company or venture whose liability towards its debts is legally limited to the extent of their investment.

37507.explanation: personal ledger is a book or a computer document in which details of money owed to or by particular people are recorded: The personal ledger will contain a separate account for each supplier and customer

37508.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37508.question_text: The sales ledger control account is also referred to as
37508.explanation: The debtors control account is also known as the sales ledger control account. This name is sometimes used for this account because it reflects the total of the business debtors or goods sold on credit

37509.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37509.question_text: An increases in the provision for doubtful debts results is a\an
37509.explanation: The higher the provision for doubtful debt, the lower the net profit at the end of the period

37510.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37510.question_text: Share of ₦3 nominal value were issued at a price ₦4. The difference of ₦1 is a
37510.explanation: Issue of shares at premium means that the issuing of shares above the face value (also called as nominal value or par value). The difference between the face value of shares and the price of shares issued at premium is the premium amount.

37512.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37512.question_text: The excess of value of assets over the purchase consideration on acquisition of a business is credited to
37512.explanation: In accounting, goodwill is the value of the business that exceeds its assets minus the liabilities.

37513.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37513.question_text: Which of the following is not the purpose of a control account?
37513.explanation:
In accounting, the controlling account (also known as an adjustment or control account) is an account in the general ledger for which a corresponding subsidiary ledger has been created. 

The details for each control account will be found in a related (but separate) subsidiary ledger. The control account keeps the general ledger free of details, but still has the correct balance for preparing the company's financial statements.

37514.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37514.question_text: Which of the following is not part of the central processing unit of a computer?
37514.explanation: Central processing unit (CPU), computer system, generally composed of the main memory, control unit, and arithmetic-logic unit.

37515.explanation: Debit provision for Depreciation account (to remove the equipment's up-to-date accumulated depreciation), Credit the account Equipment (asset disposal account) to remove the equipment's cost.

37516.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37516.question_text: Which of the following is a form of memorandum of association
37516.explanation: A memorandum of association contains a name clause, registered office clause, object (or objective clause), objects clause, liability clause, capital clause, and association clause. An MOA is a type of legal paper that is prepared when forming and registering a limited liability company (LLC).

37517.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37517.question_text: An underwriter for a company's share is paid
37517.explanation: Underwriting commission is the compensation that an underwriter receives for offering underwriting services. a fee is paid as a return for the implicit risk involved in the underwriting contract.

37518.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37518.question_text: Administrative, selling and distribution expenses in a manufacturing firm are recorded in
37518.explanation: A profit and loss (P&L) statement summarizes the revenues, costs, and expenses incurred during a specific period of time.

37519.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37519.question_text: Which of the following is not a revenue to a local government?
37519.explanation: State and local governments collect tax revenues from three primary sources: income, sales, and property taxes. Income and sales taxes make up the majority of combined state tax revenue, while property taxes are the largest source of tax revenue for local governments, including school districts.

37520.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37520.question_text: Which of the following is not an item in the profit and loss account?
37520.explanation: Drawings account is one of the temporary accounts and is closed at the end of accounting period. But this account is not closed in the income statement i.e. trading account or profit and loss account rather it is closed in the capital account of the owner which is reported in the statement of financial position

Recurrent expenditure on goods and services is expenditure, which does not result in the creation or acquisition of fixed assets (new or second-hand). 37526.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37526.question_text:
Use the following information to answer the given question.
BALANCE SHEET AS AT 31st DECEMBER, 2010
\(\begin{array}{c|c} & ₦ & & ₦ \\ \hline \text{Capital}& 40,000 & \text{Freehold premises} & 50,000\\ \text{Less: Net loss} & \frac{5,000}{35,000} & \text{Stock} & 3,000\\ \text{Less: Drawings} & \frac{2,000}{33,000} & \text{Debtors} & 4,000\\ \text{Long term loan} & \frac{20,000}{53,000} & \text{Cash at bank} & 6,500\\ \text{Creditors} & 8,000\\ \text{Accrued expenses} & \frac{4,000}{65,000} & \text{Cash in hand} & 1,500\\ & & & \text{Total 65,000}\end{array}\)
The amount of working capital is
37526.explanation:
Working capital = current assets - current liabilities

current assets= 3000 + 4000 + 6500 + 1500 = 15000

current liabilities= 8000 + 4000 = 12000

15000 - 12000 = 3000

37527.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
37527.question_text:
Use the following information to answer the given question.
BALANCE SHEET AS AT 31st DECEMBER, 2010
\(\begin{array}{c|c} & ₦ & & ₦ \\ \hline \text{Capital}& 40,000 & \text{Freehold premises} & 50,000\\ \text{Less: Net loss} & \frac{5,000}{35,000} & \text{Stock} & 3,000\\ \text{Less: Drawings} & \frac{2,000}{33,000} & \text{Debtors} & 4,000\\ \text{Long term loan} & \frac{20,000}{53,000} & \text{Cash at bank} & 6,500\\ \text{Creditors} & 8,000\\ \text{Accrued expenses} & \frac{4,000}{65,000} & \text{Cash in hand} & 1,500\\ & & & \text{Total 65,000}\end{array}\)
Working capital ratio is
37527.explanation:
The working capital ratio is calculated simply by dividing total current assets by total current liabilities.

Current assets = 3000 + 4000 +6500 + 1500 = 15000

Current liabilities = 8000 + 4000 = 12000

15000/12000 = 1.25
